product.schneider-towerat220.summary: The Tower AT that adds a 20 MB hard disk to the floppy configuration.
product.schneider-towerat220.history: Tower AT 220 offered fixed storage in Schneider's 1988 compact range, above the single- and dual-floppy versions. Its 20 MB disk and MS-DOS 3.3 / Microsoft Works package targeted everyday work. In May 1989 the press documented the 220 Mega edition, which expanded memory and floppy capacity.
product.schneider-towerat220.technical.c: The original 220 and Mega have different equipment. The Mega review describes the standard 220 with 512 KB and a 720 KB floppy drive; the 20 MB disk remains. The photograph shows a System 220 with an MM12 monitor and MF2 keyboard.
product.schneider-towerat220.technical.f: BIOS pairs have provenance attributed to a 220. MAME identifies 2.02, 1.06 and 1.01A; preserved files occupy two 32 KiB chips. It pairs EGA 1.04 with 2.02, 1.02 with 1.06 and 1.00 with 1.01. The 1.01 filenames and 1.01A label are retained as a discrepancy.
product.schneider-towerat220.warning: Historical sheet under research; booting in BluMach remains unvalidated.
product.schneider-towerat220.technical.v: Sources and file hashes have been checked. BluMach a1b0125d has no dedicated entry for this model; MAME groups Tower AT 2xx machines as not working. Booting has not been tested.
product.schneider-towerat220.technical.l: The complete machine still needs validation. Board, BIOS pair and video ROM must be identified, then POST, memory, keyboard, RTC, disks and ports tested before usable emulation can be claimed.
product.schneider-towerat220.technical.b: The CPU and memory occupy a separate card. The 201/202/220 manual documents Tower CPU286 50229, GC101/GC102 logic, DS1287 RTC and 8042/8742 keyboard controller; it includes different circuit revisions.
product.schneider-towerat220.technical.m: Expansion depends on the installed board. The manual diagram shows a 512 KB base and optional DIL/SIMM banks; it does not prove that every unit has the connectors fitted.
product.schneider-towerat220.technical.v: Integrated video leaves expansion slots available. The 1988 review documents EGA and up to 800 × 600 with a multisync monitor and suitable software; it counts three 16-bit slots and one 8-bit slot.
product.schneider-towerat220.technical.m: Schneider, Service Manual Tower AT 201/202/220, Ident-Nr. 44657, 03/1989: cover and CPU/memory diagrams reviewed; PDF preserved.
product.schneider-towerat220.technical.r: Happy Computer 11/1988, M. Ohnesorg/rz, Rechengiganten zu Niedrigpreisen, pp. 97–98 and 101: review of a Tower AT without a hard disk, with no commercial suffix identified.
product.schneider-towerat220.technical.m: Happy Computer 05/1989, Sammlerstück, p. 18: 220 Mega edition, equipment, prices and announced production run; scan and transcription preserved.
product.schneider-towerat220.technical.r: Jungsi, Schneider VGA AT System 40: range overview and approximate chronology; not a substitute for a manual covering each revision.
product.schneider-towerat220.technical.m: MAME, at.cpp: towerat2xx sets, variant provenance and unresolved EGA pairings. Files are preserved in the library; their presence does not prove universal compatibility.
product.schneider-towerat220.technical.c: BluMach a1b0125d, inspected and preserved machine table: no dedicated Tower AT entry.
